corrected_proposal.title: Federal Court Blocks Trump's Order Targeting the Minority Business Agency
corrected_proposal.description_short: EO 14238 directed MBDA to sharply reduce functions; a federal court later preliminarily enjoined implementation after staff and grant actions.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: Trump signed Executive Order 14238 on March 14, 2025, directing the Minority Business Development Agency to eliminate nonstatutory functions and reduce statutory operations and staffing to the legal minimum. The Rhode Island federal court later recorded that most MBDA staff were placed on leave and grants appeared terminated, then granted a preliminary injunction. This account corrects the February date and does not claim all federal minority-business support ended.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On March 14, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14238, directing the Minority Business Development Agency to eliminate nonstatutory functions to the maximum extent allowed by law and reduce statutory work and staffing to the legal minimum. Afterward, MBDA placed all but five employees on paid administrative leave, and the district court said the agency appeared to have terminated its existing grants. In its May 6 preliminary order, the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island stated that the executive order, as carried out, violated the Administrative Procedure Act in an arbitrary and capricious way and disregarded Congress’s role in authorizing agencies and appropriating funds. The court granted a preliminary injunction against implementing the order at MBDA. That was a preliminary ruling, not a final merits judgment. The records do not show that all federal minority-business support or SBA programs ended, or establish later agency operations after the injunction.
organization_tags: U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island

source_fact_map.fact: The court granted the states' motion for a preliminary injunction concerning EO implementation at MBDA.
source_fact_map.quote: the Court GRANTS the States’ motion.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Plaintiffs are twenty-one states (the “States”) who move for a preliminary injunction, seeking to restrain the Defendants from implementing the President’s Executive Order 14238, “Continuing the Reduction of the Federal Bureaucracy” (“Reduction EO”), as it applies to three federal agencies—the Institute of Museum and Library Services (“IMLS”), the Minority Business Development Agency (“MBDA”), and the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service (“FMCS”). The Defendants oppose the motion on various jurisdictional grounds and assert that the States have not satisfied the elements required for entitlement to preliminary relief. For the reasons stated below, the Court GRANTS the States’ motion.

source_fact_map.fact: The Rhode Island Attorney General reported that a preliminary injunction order was entered to stop the agencies' dismantling.
source_fact_map.quote: a Rhode Island court entered a preliminary injunction order to stop the dismantling of three federal agencies
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Attorney General Neronha today announced that a Rhode Island court entered a preliminary injunction order to stop the dismantling of three federal agencies that provide services and funding supporting public libraries and museums, workers, and small businesses nationwide.

source_fact_map.fact: The court stated in its preliminary order that EO 14238, as carried out, violated the APA as arbitrary and capricious and disregarded Congress's role.
source_fact_map.quote: This Executive Order violates the Administrative Procedures Act (“APA”) in the arbitrary and capricious way it was carried out.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Once again, this Court is confronted with a legal challenge by various states, against an Executive Order that attempts to dismantle congressionally sanctioned agencies and ignores congressionally appropriated funds. Here, the targeted federal agencies support our libraries, museums, minority business enterprises, and the well-respected federal mediation services. This Executive Order violates the Administrative Procedures Act (“APA”) in the arbitrary and capricious way it was carried out. It also disregards the fundamental constitutional role of each of the branches of our federal government; specifically, it ignores the unshakable principles that Congress makes the law and appropriates funds, and the Executive implements the law Congress enacted and spends the funds Congress appropriated.

impact_proposal.confidence_reason: The executive directive and court-recorded staff/grant actions are sourced to official records, while the injunction and court assessment were preliminary and later operations are not established here.
impact_proposal.rationale: The order triggered a major staff reduction and apparent termination of MBDA grants, and the court’s preliminary order expressly found that the EO, as carried out, violated the APA in an arbitrary and capricious way. That court finding supports a serious procedural-abuse estimate, while remaining preliminary rather than a final liability judgment. A nationwide agency was affected; the preliminary injunction interrupted implementation, and no private benefit is shown.
basis: EO 14238 named MBDA; court record described most staff placed on leave and grants apparently terminated; a preliminary injunction followed.
